name: antarii-spike-fit-throwaway
description: Disposable spike: the ADR-003 fit spike and the ADR-005 evaluator-hosting spike. Not a component repository.

comment: 🔴 expo-camera IS EXCLUDED FROM THE APPLE BUILD ONLY, AND IT IS THE FIX
FOR A LAUNCH CRASH RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.
On 2026-10-29 the iPhone 13 died ~19 ms after launch, before any
application code: dyld 'Symbol missing', AnyModule._classTypes, referenced
from ExpoCamera.framework and expected in ExpoModulesCore.framework
(crash report AntariiSpike-2026-10-29-220427.ips). The eleven expo-*
packages are hand-pinned at mismatched patch levels — expo 58.0.11, whose
one nested expo-modules-core is 58.0.19, beside expo-camera 58.0.14, which
constrains the core not at all: its only peer is "expo": "*".
⚠ SCOPED TO apple ON PURPOSE. Android has no Swift ABI, its build carries
expo-camera and runs, and SC-04's scanner is proven there. Excluding it
for both platforms would discard a working capability to fix the other's
defect.
➕ This is the isolation NOT_PROBED_TODAY asked for and we then broke:
'the only new native package in scope, isolated to its own build step
because F-12 is unexplained and one package keeps blame attributable'.
SC-04 and SC-10 shipped together, so a camera defect first presented as a
possible Rust-hosting failure — a finding that would have gone to ADR-005.
✕ TEMPORARY. The real fix is aligning the expo-* versions, after which
this key comes out and iOS barcode is answered properly.
ⓘ The key path is read from the installed source, not recalled:
expo-modules-autolinking/build/commands/autolinkingOptions.js:72-79 reads
expo.autolinking, then expo.autolinking[platform] where platform is
'apple' or 'android' (falling back to 'ios' when 'apple' is absent).
